searchText: Here's what <@206016661470314496> had to day about it > > When downloading headers, the only way to do it concurrently is to download fixed chunks, and then piece the chunks together > Everything else we can just fill whatever's delivered based on the headr chain > but with the header chain. itself, there;s nothing to map it onto > so dynamic chunks would make the code very complex > we retrieve 512 headers in one chunk > We could retrieve less, but then sync gets slow due to latency issues > I don't remember how large a header is, but the idea is to try and have 256-512KB network packets > downloader docs say a header is 500B > so 500 headers == 256KB > that seems like a sane default > bodies and receipts are large, so capping them makes sense > capping headers (at 192) makes a lot less sense imo seems reasonable, and it is not a big deal to bump Besu's max header limit. It was just a surprising requirement. I will check with folks who know more about the alternative consensus mechanism header sizes to see if the 192 limit is something to do with ibft or qbft. however, for the sake of testing the PR, I bumped to 512 and it seems to progress. Geth is dropping besu with a handshake issue, but hopefully will have good results soon.

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content:
Here's what <@206016661470314496> had to day about it

> 
> When downloading headers, the only way to do it concurrently is to download fixed chunks, and then piece the chunks together
> Everything else we can just fill whatever's delivered based on the headr chain
> but with the header chain. itself, there;s nothing to map it onto
> so dynamic chunks would make the code very complex
> we retrieve 512 headers in one chunk
> We could retrieve less, but then sync gets slow due to latency issues 
> I don't remember how large a header is, but the idea is to try and have 256-512KB network packets
> downloader docs say a header is 500B
> so 500 headers == 256KB
> that seems like a sane default
> bodies and receipts are large, so capping them makes sense
> capping headers (at 192) makes a lot less sense imo

excerpts.author: suburbandad_
excerpts.content:
seems reasonable, and it is not a big deal to bump Besu's max header limit.  It was just a surprising requirement.  I will check with folks who know more about the alternative consensus mechanism header sizes to see if the 192 limit is something to do with ibft or qbft.  

however, for the sake of testing the PR, I bumped to 512 and it seems to progress.  Geth is dropping besu with a handshake issue, but hopefully will have good results soon.
